text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Cheese Blend Powder Certified Gluten Free Long Term Food Storage Everyday Meal Prep Large Can, 1.48 kg I buy Augason products when they are on sale. Been doing this on and off for a few years now. Always been a bit of a "prepper", since I was a toddler it seems, haha (In my 40s now). I has served me well through power outages, sicknesses, unemployment, and even bigger stuff like the pandemic, and now... *vaguely gestures around* everything else that is going on. I've never been one to be without when anything has come up. I never did "emergency food" if only because I didnt have the budget. I would stick with typical foods and try to store them well. Well now I have a little more wiggle room in my budget, and with the on and off sales of long term storage (20+ years), I take advantage when I can. I remember buying some Augason eggs back in 2019 for $19. Today? $33-56 for same container, depending on the day.

And so, I haven't opened this 3lbs 4 ounce container of cheese blend powder.. sorry. I dont intend to any time soon. But I wanted to shore up my options. Having some soups and such just adds flavor to other options used. I can add more veg, or a protein, or beans, or simply have some bread to dip into it. Or I can use as way to flavor something. I have a slew of reviews to write on various Augason products, and so they will all be pretty much the same: Super long term storage (25+ years), no matter what the weight, it will be stuffed into a #10 can (that reads, "number ten", not ten pound. I see that mistake in reviews). They keep sizes uniform. Next size up is a round bucket, next size up gets into the rectangular buckets. This is for storage that can be uniform, etc. So yes, you may buy a 7 ounce item that is volume wise that takes up a smidge of space, but it will be packed into a large #10 container. Just remember, all food products are sold based on weight, not volume anyway. All of my containers have been in perfect condition. Maybe one day soon I will try one container out and see how the product actually is.

Everyone's SHTF scenario varies. It could be bad weather (tornadoes, hurricanes, blizzards, ice storms), could be illness, could be road trip gone wrong (you do keep supplies in your car too, right?!), could be unemployment, or power outage, or lack of transportation, or oven/fridge/other appliance break down, or bigger stuff like plagues, food shortages, supply chain issues, *cough WW3 cough*, etc. No matter the situation we all need some things to get by: we need is food, water, shelter, some hygeine and medical stuff, and so on. You dont have to stack "emergency supplies" but you do need to stack shelf stable food items. Buy a few extra things every single time you go to the store. If you get to a spot that you feel comfortable and have the budget, then grab the "emergency" items like Augason offers. I like adding it in and just forgetting about it.

IFAK Trauma First Aid Kit, Micro Rip Away Molle Med Pouch, Fully Stocked Small Tactical Medical Bag with Tourniquet for Military Camping Hiking I picked up 4 of these for Christmas gifts for friends and family. The pouch is a great size, quality is good and holds a lot more than what is included once you take the TQ out and mount it. The shears are a great starter/smaller set, not flimsy like others I have found in other kits. The TQ is your standard CAT clone. I've purchased a lot of different ones from other manufacturers around, and the one provided is the best of the cheaper clones that I have found. With those clones I can get occlusion quickly and easily on both upper arm and thigh placement on large (250lb +) and smaller (95lb) sized people. The windless will hold up well, its is well made and strong. The compressed gauze is a great little addition to this bag as well. The Israeli bandage is well made, vacuum packed and does not need to be opened and "staged" like some that are sewen through. The tactical pen is very heavy and a nice rollerball style refil, the glass break on the back is very sharp and appears to be tool steel or high carbon.
I added about $15 worth of add-ons to make it complete Bleed/IFAK. A pair of chest seals, additional rolled gauze, some 4x4's, some tape and an "ouch pouch" consisting of some band-aids, sting pads, loperamide and Benadryl. Even with the added items, there is still room for more in the kit if needed. I did go through and vacuum seal all of the items I added other than the ouch pouch as I do in all my IFAKs I build for spaace and to keep things clean.
I noticed that I bought these when they were deeply discounted at $24 each, and if they drop down to that price again I will be buying more.

Gamo Swarm Maxxim Air Rifle I cant find my original review so Im making a new one.

Ive purchase Gamo rifles for years so I was excited to see a break-barrel repeater. Well, the concept is good. I have had nothing but issues with this gun after about 8 months. The biggest issues I was having was surrounding the rotary magazine. At first, i was having issues seating the pellets properly in the magazines. They just arent user friendly and are difficult to sit them flush. If they dont sit flush they may not make contact with the hammer. After a while the magazines were no longer advancing correctly and the pellet would not rotate into position. I then purchased several new magazines. They all worked fine the first couple times and then soon after they had the same rotational issue. It seems to be a know problem with no known cure. Gamo created something nice. It would be nice of it worked properly. Avoid the headaches and just get a single-shot break-barrel until Gamo figures it out.
text_fidelity_b: Gamo Swarm Maxxim Air Rifle

This helped make my ice last even longer. After 4 days of use it finally thawed. I did how ever notice it didnt seal to bottom of cooler. Meaning water will get to the other side as ice melts. So if your using the divider for dry side wet side it isnt going to work. You will have to make some type of seal between the two sides to have any chance of keeping 1 side dry.
But if your using just to help ice stay froze longer this is so perfect for that use.

I love my cooler and it will pay for itself within 40 days of using just off the ice savings.

This worked perfectly for my new 65 quart Kenai Cooler.. apperently the Grizzley Company owns Kenai as well judging by the pamphlet provided with cooler, so there wasnt much research needed to find one to fit.

There is a few lbs of weight (unfrozen) for it to be less then an inch thick, it's also very rugged, I'm sure it could take a drop or two and shouldnt have any issues. It fit perfectly inside the center divider groove and has about 1.5" left from top inside lip.
There is a drain plug on the ice pack for replacement liquid. The pack is thin enough it will freeze pretty quick but it does have some size to it so freezer space may or could be an issue. This will help to precool your cooler before use so you can get the maximum duration of chill out of you high dollar purchase and use it to keep you cup ice seperate from chilling ice that hands, cans touch everytime its opened.

If you find this review helpful, please vote, so Amazonian browsers can better learn, research and understand how products work for them.!. Thank you and Happy Buying

text_fidelity_a:
Light My Fire Swedish FireSteel 2.0 Scout 3,000 Strike Fire Starter with Emergency Whistle I had a couple older magnesium stick fire starter for years and was really excited to try this out. Most people I've listened to swear by them.
Here are the PROs:
- This performs medium to well for giving you a spark. Having never used one (and probably using poor technique), I was still able to generate a decent spark at least 1 out of every 2-3 strikes.
- Doubles as a whistle. This thing actually works extremely well. If you ever need it, it's simple and high-pitched, a great space-saver.
- Feels good to use. I'd rate it at around 6 out of 10. It's a little short and I found the striker attached to the steel via the cord a little restricting, but the thumb grooves make up for it. It's funny how a small depression in plastic can make that much of a difference in comfort.

Here are the CONs:
- This requires that you have good tender or some type of fuel/accelerant. I miss having my pile of magnesium scrapings to be honest. While it's another piece of equipment, I'm probably going to keep my magnesium stick with me. It seems like the majority of times I've gone packing or camping, it's been damp out, and finding a decent amount of usable tender isn't always a sure bet.
- A little small. This is my complaint with just about any striker. They're just about a 1/4"-1/5" too small to be really comfortable. This is being picky, but still worth mentioning.

Overall, I'm enjoying using this thing and I'll probably make it a mainstay of my gear.
text_fidelity_b: Light My Fire Swedish FireSteel 2.0 Scout 3,000 Strike Fire Starter with Emergency Whistle

text_fidelity_a:
DEERFAMY Easy Pop Up Tent, 3 Person Pop Up Tent for Camping, Tent Instant Pop Up with Vestibule Army Green Pop Up Camping Tent for Family Ok, let's get something straight- there's no way 3-4 adults are fitting in this thing. But that's normal for tent ratings- they are usually a little bit generous with their occupancy rating and assume bodies are stacked like sardines inside. But this is more like half capacity at best- I'd say maybe 2 adults, or one adult and 2 kids. However, that did NOT stop 3 of my kids from wanting to run inside the very second it popped open. They fit comfortably inside and honestly it makes a great kid's tent if you want, for example, to have a separate adults' tent or even just let the kids have a backyard sleepover. We haven't used it in the rain yet so I can't vouch for that sort of use, but I CAN say that it pops open effortlessly by just removing it from the bag it comes in. Easiest tent install ever! Putting it back in? That's a challenge.
I like that it comes with directions sewn into the bag, but they were still hard to follow if you haven't done a tent fold like this before. It is similar to those car windshield pop up protectors in that it has plastic circular hoops that need to fold along itself to make a large oval into smaller circles. And if you make a mistake, it will POP open in your face and make you start over. That was annoying. But I did eventually get it to the correct size folding on the third try, and was able to get it back in the back and zip it up.
At $70, you can get a much bigger tent from Coleman or Ozark Trail, but not a pop up kind like this one. The instant pop ups fetch a premium, and I recall the last one I saw was slightly bigger than this one but nearly 2x the price, so I think it is priced appropriately for what it is. I'd consider this one a good value, I just wish it was easier to put away, and was a little more realistic about capacity.
text_fidelity_b: DEERFAMY Easy Pop Up Tent, 3 Person Pop Up Tent for Camping, Tent Instant Pop Up with Vestibule Army Green Pop Up Camping Tent for Family

text_fidelity_a:
Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow Good anti stress eye pillow. What I like about the Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy pillow
1) I like the fragrance of the lavender and chamomile pillow.
2) The fragrance is not overwhelming it is subtle.
3) It is not overstuffed so it drapes nicely over your eye and sinus area when you are lying flat.
4) The silk has a cooling effect
5) I have chronic sinusitis and this pillow feels like it helps to relieve some of that tight pressure pain. It also seems to calm the area around my eyes.
I have used several different sinus pillow type remedies over the years for that "ahhh relief!" moment when you can feel the swelling and ache diminishing.Not many were very effective but this one and the Lavender eye pillow by AyaZen are both effective. However, I would choose the one from AyaZen over this one because:
1) It can be heated and froze as long as you put it in a plastic sealed bag so it doesn't absorb freezer odor.
2) It has more filling and a more balanced filling making it a little weightier than the Earth Therapeutics eye pillow
3) The velvet like cover of the AyaZen is soft and luxurious yet it also has a griping effect so it doesn't readily slip off your face.
4) It has a stronger lavender scent that is soothing but not overwhelming.
5) For me, this pillow relieves the pain and pressure associated with my sinusitis better.

As a comparison, they are both good eye pillows but AyaZen wins for me.

The reason Earth Therapeutics is not a perfect five stars and doesn't win for me:
1) It doesn't have the balanced filling the AyaZen does
2) The silk used to encase the Earth Therapeutics pillow slips very easily unless you are lying down flat.If your head happens to turn a little while sleeping at an angle or with your head raised at any height, it slips off. Even though you can conform it to your eyes and nose it won't stay because of the silkiness of the material and the almost whisper light weight of the pillow. If your head is raised at any angle or your head happens to fall sideways while napping, you must continually reposition the pillow.
3) you cannot heat it in the microwave or put it in the freezer. I know this pillow is suppose to be Therapeutic based solely on the oils it harbors and the silk that encases it but it just needs a little more to really reach that Therapeutic level.

I bought this based on it conforming to the face and being Therapeutic. However, I often sleep with my head raised up or in my recliner because of breathing issues due to my sinuses.The silk of this pillow would always cause it to slip down or sideways causing me to wake up and recenter it on my eyes. Overall, I would recommend this pillow for someone who doesn't have to sleep with the head or upper body raised at any height and doesn't have to turn their head much while napping. The silk does have a cooling effect and the lavender and chamomile does help to relieve some of the pressure and pain.
text_fidelity_b: Earth Therapeutics Mind/Body Therapy Anti-Stress Eye Pillow, Lavender + Chamomile, 1 pillow

Where things get a bit more premium and specialized are the Kip Leather baseball gloves. These can be found in both USA Kip Leather and Japanese Kip Leather. Kip leather is usually the most preferred leather among professional players due to the light, firm, feel and higher quality of the leather. Kip leather comes from younger cattle, which creates a lighter hide that is extremely durable and taut, while also being a little bit easier to break in when compared to USA premium steerhide gloves.

Selecting Your Leather:

Cowhide Leather - Heavy leather, fastest break in time, medium quality, short durability, ideal for youth players.

Steerhide Leather - Heaviest leather, longest break in time, high quality, longest durability, ideal for high school and college players.

Kip Leather - Lighter leather, medium break in time, higher quality, long durability, ideal for college and pro players.

Japanese Kip Leather - Lightest leather, medium break in time, highest quality, long durability, ideal for elite pro players.

POLAR Ft1 Heart Rate Monitor I decided I wanted a Polar heart rate monitor as I've used their HRMs before and was happier with them than with some other brands. Right now I'm on a bit of a budget, so decided to go with the lower-featured FT1. I have to say I have been pleasantly surprised. After a little learning curve with the 1-button controls, I've found it easy to use, informative and the audible alarm is helpful.

The only thing I didn't love about my Polar FT1 was the chest strap it comes with. The higher end Polars come with a softer fabric strap, but the FT1 comes with a strap with a sort of flexible plastic piece on the front that isn't as form-fitting. It's not terrible - honest! - but it's not great, either. I ended up getting a Polar H7, and it works great with my FT1 plus I can simultaneously use it with various fitness apps on my phone; I like it best with Endomondo, which also sends your workout to My Fitness Pal.

The features I was looking for that the FT1 has:
A large-ish, easy to read display
An alarm you can set so you're alerted when your heart rate gets too high or too low during workouts
The ability to change your max heart rate
Comfortable wrist band

Overall I'm happy with my FT1, and even happier when I paired it with the Polar H7, but honestly it works fine with the strap it came with. I may upgrade someday, but for now my FT1 has/does everything I need and works great.
text_fidelity_b: POLAR Ft1 Heart Rate Monitor

text_fidelity_a:
Srixon Men's Z Cabretta Leather Golf Glove This is a soft, flexible glove that fits comfortably. It is not the most expensive golf glove you could purchase, by any means, and if you prefer not to use leather, it is possible instead to purchase a golf glove made of synthetic leather.

Since there is zero information about this product posted on this Amazon product page, I am including a product description taken from the Srixon website:

"Lycra insert positioned across the knuckles. Cabretta leather for ideal fit and feel. Provides flexibility and added comfort. The Srixon Z-STAR Premium Cabretta gloves use only the highest quality leather to ensure consistent fit and feel. The Cabrex-Esx tanning process uses hybrid resins to maintain the leather's original softness, preventing any hardening of the cabretta leather."

As stated above in the company information, this Srixon golfing glove is made of cabretta leather. The company makes four different gloves, the All-Weather Glove which is their least expensive glove, this particular glove, the Z Star Premium Cabretta Glove which is about 50% more expensive than this glove, and a Rain Glove which is the most expensive glove Srixon makes.

As the name of the product suggests, this glove is made from cabretta leather. Cabretta leather is a particularly soft and pliable leather which is quite strong. It is processed to have a smooth, luxurious finish and, in addition, Srixon coats the cabretta leather it uses with "hybrid resins," in order to maintain the leather's softness without need for additional treatment by the glove's owner. Hybrid resins are a cold-manufactured blend of polyesters, vinyl esters, polyurethanes or epoxies and therefore may give off a strong odor in addition to the normal odors that leather emits due to the chemicals used in the tanning and dyeing processes.

The source of cabretta leather is the hides of "hair sheep," also known as "naked sheep." This type of sheep either does not grow wool or grows a mixture of hair and wool. In each case, the sheep naturally sheds, removing the necessity for shearing, which is a big expense for wool sheep. Hair sheep are raised primarily in the tropics, and increasingly in the USA. They are more hardy and disease resistant than wool sheep and they do well in hot and humid climates. Examples of two popular breeds in the USA are the Dorper and the St. Croix:

The Dorper breed was developed in South Africanis in the 1930's primarily as a meat sheep. It has a mixed, hair-wool coat, and its skin is prized for leatherwork and comprises over 20% of the value of the sheep.

The St. Croix breed is a descendant of the hair sheep of West Africa and was first imported into the USA in 1975. It sheds it's mixed wool-hair coat in the spring.

Srixon Sports USA is primarily known for golf balls, and to a lesser extent for other golf equipment, including its four types of golf gloves. SRI Sports Limited owns both the Cleveland and Srixon golf brands, and in 2008 began global distribution of its products.

Srixon Sports USA is based in Georgia. I could not, however, discover where its products are manufactured. There is no information about this on their website. But given the fact that the company is not shouting to the skies that its products are "made in the USA," I would imagine this product is manufactured in China, India, Thailand or the like. This is unfortunate because there are over 66 leather manufacturing companies right here in the USA. How do I know that? I looked it up, just like I looked up everything I could find out about this company.
text_fidelity_b: Srixon Men's Z Cabretta Leather Golf Glove

text_fidelity_a:
FILA Accessories Agility Kit I have had a desire to improve my agility, having done regular exercises as a kid. I wanted to start again, so got this set. Let's take a look at this set.

WHAT IS THIS SET LIKE?
CASE
First of all, this set comes in a nice carry case. It shuts with a spring loaded clamp and has a string for carrying or hanging up.

INSTRUCTIONS
There are instruction lists in this kit. First there are general instructions. Then there are instruction sheets with photos for each piece in this kit. I highly recommend putting each of these in a clear presentation sleeve to keep them clean, in one piece and easy to refer to.

This set comes with three types of props to ;help with exercising to develop agility:
AGILITY CONES
These cones essentially work for markers in setting up various exercises. Some of the activities are to run through and are done on your feet. Others are done with shuffling and bending to touch them. The cones are close to the ground and have a hole in the middle for grass to pop through if necessary.

AGILITY HURDLES
These are low to the ground and you set them up to do various running, stepping, and hopping over in various ways. These are tubular blue plastic with black plastic caps on the ends. These are not overly sturdy and if it is a windy day, they tend to migrate if not on the grass or other rougher surface. There is a web belt that you use to keep them together when not in use that has velcro on the ends.

AGILITY LADDER
This is a web ladder. There are hooks included to hold the ladder into place on the ground. There are exercises for hopping, skipping, running, and shuffling.

CAUTION
There are cautions provided with each exercise sheet to help those who might be a bit over ambitious not to over do it too fast.

HOW DID THIS WORK OUT FOR ME?
I was able to use this for a while to increase my agility. When we got a rainy season I could not do it anymore, and now it is winter, so I am waiting for spring again. On a gym floor these would not be as nice- they would easily slide out of place and I would spend more time fixing them than using them. I prefer using these on the grass or dirt.

This is a decent starter set. Once you get committed to using it, you can move up to something a bit more intense. However, this is easy to take with you and transport to keep you going when you have to leave and go on vacation or somewhere else for business, etc.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a great basic set that is best used on grass or ground, this set helps develop basic agility skills. It can also be brought on vacation or business trips to keep in shape if that is needed, as it is small enough to take with you if you have room for it.

MY RATING
FOUR stars. It is not quite as practical to use on anywhere but grass/ground, but it is decent and I like the way it packs away to take with me.
text_fidelity_b: FILA Accessories Agility Kit

Hydration Belt for Running - Includes Accessories and Two 10-Ounce BPA-Free and Leak-Proof Water Bottles : A Bounce-Free & Lightweight Fuel Gear While hydration packs are very useful to have, they tend to look more like medical support equipment or, at best, just plain geeky. This one, however, dials the geek factor way down. Not completely, but it's well done.

The build quality is excellent. The belt itself is neoprene that is well-stitched and assembled. It feels very solid and able to withstand more than an ample amount of punishment. The waist straps are elastic which is far better than the usual web material since it stretches easily to maintain its position in use without rubbing your skin raw from bouncing around. The elastic is also covered with a sort of felt-type material. Both the straps and the belt itself are very comfortable to wear -- zero problems with movement.

The bottles fit into neoprene holsters that hold them firmly. I had zero issues with the bottles coming out when using this, but still had no problems taking the bottles out when I needed a drink. Getting them back into the holsters took a little more effort, but with some practice it became a one-handed operation. The bottles are square-ish in shape to keep them from sticking out too much when you're wearing the belt.

The front of the belt has a small pocket to stash a phone (or anything else). It has a zipper opening that operates easily and smoothly. I would have liked to see a somewhat larger zipper pull tab, but the current system works well.

The bottles are very soft - I'm going to guess they are made of HDPE since they are so easy to squeeze. They stand upright without any problem when taken out of the holster, and have a wide fill top for easy under-the-faucet filling. They have a pull-top for use that is a bit stiff to pull out, but it does seal well when closed. You do need to be careful about squeezing the bottle too much when taking a drink since the water comes out so quickly that you'll make a mess. But, that also adds to the cooling, and once you get the squeeze level down it's not an issue.

Overall, this is a very nicely made belt. It doesn't fully eliminate the geek factor of a hydration pack, but it does dial it down to an acceptable level, and has a lot of nice design touches to make it comfortable and easy to use. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Hydration Belt for Running - Includes Accessories and Two 10-Ounce BPA-Free and Leak-Proof Water Bottles : A Bounce-Free & Lightweight Fuel Gear

When I contacted Gaiam about the DVD, they sent me a replacement. Happily, it was different one that was more suited to my health, a beginner's workout done by a blonde woman named Suzanne. Vivid Sports Rainbow Graphite Pickleball Paddle Set, Polymer Honeycomb Core, 1 Neoprene Paddle Cover, Paddle for Men, Women, Children, Supporting The Human Rights Organization, USA Pickleball Approved This is an OK paddle. I don't love it, I don't hate it. I think my favorite thing about this paddle is the colorful design on the paddle face.

The face itself has almost no texture/grit, which as a brand new player may not matter, but will quickly become important after you get the hang of hitting the ball. The paddle face is approximately ~0.5 inches (~13 mm), which is on the thinner side. The upside of a thin paddle is that it provides more power than a thicker paddle, but on the downside, it will be tougher to spin with it (which is compounded by the fact the paddle face has no texture).

Another thing I didn't like was the handle--it feels flat, like a piece of wood. Round handles are much more comfortable in my experience. The grip, however, was pretty nice. It is soft and comfortable to hold, and absorbs sweat pretty well. An added bonus with this paddle is that it comes with a paddle cover. Not a huge deal, but a nice touch nonetheless.

My bottom line is that this is a decent first paddle. Otherwise, I would pass.

text_fidelity_a:
Ringside Pro Style IMF Tech Boxing Training Sparring Gloves We just purchased a super tall, somewhat more slender than usual cylindrical punching bag from the same brand, and so were looking for a good set of starter punching gloves that would allow us to have fun with our new fitness toy. In the past, I've had a brand of punching gloves (which I brought with me to the gym) that I didn't like so much, because there was an uncomfortable seam that hit right about where my fingernails were, so every time I would get punching, a few minutes in and my fingertips would start feeling a little sore and bruised. Yet I didn't want to spend a great deal of money on something that would only be used for probably 30 minutes a day at most.

So I was very excited to be offered this set of 18 ounce midrange punching gloves for review, because they seemed like the perfect middle-of-the-road option. Indeed, not only do these fit my size small women's hands, but they also fit my husband's hands comfortably, and he usually wears a size medium to large. If you have very large hands, you might find these a little tight, but for the size hands that we have, and the fact that we were hoping to be able to share them despite having a pretty big difference in our hand size, these are perfect.

The material and stitching seem high quality, and I like the fit, which is compressive enough that they do not slide around yet not so tight that either of us feels our circulation is being cut off. The seaming is perfect, and there are no places where seam falls in an awkward or uncomfortable place on my hands. I like that the material over the hand is matte rather than shiny, as the shiny material on my last one sometimes had an effect on how the glove slid, or didn't, across the punching bag.

The molded foam provides good protection, and overall these are such a huge notch nicer than the ones that were half the price that I would expect them to be priced higher than they are. While I have never personally gotten to try the more expensive ones made for people who are more serious about MMA or boxing, for people who enjoy just a casual work out with the punching bag, I think these are the nicest ones you could possibly need. We've been super impressed by them.
text_fidelity_b: Ringside Pro Style IMF Tech Boxing Training Sparring Gloves

I had not heard of Old Timer until recently, but their knives look nice and I thought I would give them a chance. So far I am very pleased with this particular knife.

This is a no-frills knife that doesn't try to get too fancy. The blades have to be pulled open manually without a spring assist, and it does not have some of the things that other knives frequently have such as a corkscrew, screwdriver and other integrated emergency tools. Instead it has three blades - nothing more. Each blade is different and has different uses, though the thought that comes to mind when I look at the knife as a whole is whittling and carving.

The blades are tight and do not wobble. That's a good thing and says that the knife as a whole is assembled well. The blades feel solid and secure when opened.

I love the bone handle. It feels good in the hand and it looks retro which is a good thing. The texture makes it easy to maintain a grip, even when hands are just a little wet.

This is a smallish knife, so it will fit in your pocket and not take up lots of room. This is a little smaller than most knives I am used to carrying, and that's a mixed bag to me - on one hand I like having a larger knife, probably because I am used to having one, but on the other I like the fact that it is small, compact and lightweight.

This is a very nice knife that sticks to getting the basics right without a bunch of extras that only add weight and take away from the overall package. It looks great and is made well.

Cooler Shock Ice Packs for Cooler, Strong, Reusable, Premium Ice Pack and Lunch Cooler Set for Long Term Use, Cools Faster Than Ice, 3 Pack Product review: this was my second order of these.

Pros:

1. Cost: Very affordable, especially when comparing to the Yeti and RTIC packs

2. They work: they freeze colder than ordinary ice packs and last longer as well. I have a 60L rotomolded South Jetty Cooler (southjettycoolers.com). Put a number of these in my cooler this past Monday. The packs, while no longer frozen (4 days later), are very very cold. More importantly the beverages in the cooler are still frosty cold.

3. Ease of Set-Up. These are mailed without any liquid in them. There is a chemical in the pouches, that when mixed with water turns into a gel. The directions were clear and it was very easy to fill the piouches up with the required amount of water, get the air out, zip shut, dry the fold by the zip top and iron to seal. If someone is not comfortable with filling and sealing these ice packs themselves, I believe you can ordered them filled for an additional cost.

4. Space Saving: Since the exterior is not a hard molded plastic bottle, these are smaller and more flexible. Which makes them fit in the cooler better. The pouches as a very heavy duty Mylar too pouch. They feel as though they're pretty strong.

Bottom Line: I would HIGHLY recommend these for your cooler. I have yet to come up with a Con. If I do, I will revise my review accordingly.

Update 17Jun18: I’ve been using these for nearly 1.5 years now. At one time I had 7 of these in various sizes. Today, I still have 5. What does that mean to me, it means they’re durable. I use these a lot while hunting, fishing, boating, & traveling. They hold up well and will start to delaminate over time. But for the cost savings and convenience over ice, that’s OK; they’re made of a Mylar packaging, not Kevlar. I will definitely order more of these soon.

SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black There is a major difference between this tube and its non thorn-resistant counterparts. The difference translates to a 3x larger package and a 3x stiffer inner tube. Whether this means that it will intercede on your behalf when penetrating objects attempt to derail your day, time will tell. But I can tell you that:

1) It takes some effort to stuff this piece of salami into your tire. It doesn't bend willingly.
2) It takes some getting used to on the road. Your tire will absorb less shock from road imperfections, resulting in a harsh ride. It's not like riding on solid rubber, but it's not as soft as a regular inner tube.

In my opinion, the harsh ride is worth it on a daily commuter, where reliability is paramount. I'm not sure if I'd use this on a recreational bike. A suspension bike may be fine.

Update: after a week or two, I stopped noticing the stiffer ride quality. Also, I have about 50lbs extra on that rear wheel, so my experience may not be typical (it's an e-bike).
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black

OGIO Corp City [[VIDEOID:fbaddcf27c139f6513397e4ac2d8e8a0]] I love this Ogio bag! It's probably the most functional thing that I own. I'm on my second Ogio City Corp bag, because I loved the first one so much. And, the first one took four years of daily pounding, many airplane flights, literally tons of books, computers, and other things being hauled all over everywhere.

This bag has tons of pockets, and they're all extremely accessible. I love how easy my laptop is to remove when I'm taking a flight and they make me take it out of my bag. I can cram loads of stuff into this bag. This bag will get too heavy far before it gets too full. I think that it says it carries a 17" laptop, but I'm sure you could get a 19" laptop in here if you're fine with a tight squeeze.

Like I said, my first one of these bags wore out after 4 years of daily use. The reason it wore out is that there was a ton of pressure on the zipper from opening it under strain with a lot of heavy stuff in it. If you take better care of your bag than I did, you could expect this to last 10+ years of daily use.

Pros:
+Has tons of pockets. I didn't even have time on my video to go over all of the pockets and features.
+It took me over four years of daily heavy use to wear out the zipper on my first one
+Extremely high quality
+Great for a travel bag for the airplane. It's very easy to take my laptop out.
+Shoulder strap is very comfortable, even for long distance walking

Cons:
-One of the pockets has a bottom zipper, and it sometimes comes unzipped
text_fidelity_b: OGIO Corp City

text_fidelity_a:
YEEPSYS Portable Collapsible Camping Bucket Outdoor Basin Folding Foot Soak Tub Multifunctional Foldable Water Container for Fishing Travel Camping Hiking Foot Soaking Bath Car Washing I have another one of [[ASIN:B091GF5B46 these]] type foot baths and fell in love with it so much that I wanted another one.

In the package is one carry pouch and one very small outdoor foot bath. The basin is fully collapsible and very small.  I unfolded it completely and made sure the edge of the basin was standing up.

As can be seen by my photos, I actually used this indoors and it worked. I had to be careful not to let water flow over the edge. This is really for outdoor use only. To ensure the water stays inside, I only filled it several inches, enough to soak up to the base of my ankles.

Once I was done, I rinsed the bath out. There was a water spot on my floor because the bottom of the basin gets wet when in the sink--another reason this should be used outdoors. Note that it takes many hours for this basin to dry. 

I was actually going to rate this 4 stars like I did my other one because it operates exactly the same. However, the purple color of this bath bled all over my towels and I could not rinse the color out. It destroyed my towels.

In summary, this foot bath is portable and does work as long as one is careful. However, this can be repurposed as an ice bucket with drinks for a picnic or to hold small beach toys for the kids. At the current price of $7.99, this is more expensive than the one I already own. It is not great but does somewhat serve the purpose it was intended for. What I love about this is that I do not have to carry a heavy pail to bathe my feet. Also, it folds down nicely. This would have received 4 stars from me if it were not for the color bleed. I cannot recommend this due to that issue and my recommendation would be to purchase this [[ASIN:B091GF5B46 one]] instead. Not only is that one cheaper but there is no color bleed.

UPDATE: I washed the towels twice that this bucket bled on and the color DID NOT come out. This is such a BIG NEGATIVE. Even if using this outdoors, the color will bleed all over--one's clothes, the camper floor, the towels, etc.
text_fidelity_b: YEEPSYS Portable Collapsible Camping Bucket Outdoor Basin Folding Foot Soak Tub Multifunctional Foldable Water Container for Fishing Travel Camping Hiking Foot Soaking Bath Car Washing

text_fidelity_a:
LED Bike Lights Set -OBDKCAN USB Rechargeable 300LM Waterproof Front Headlight and 100LM Tail Light Including 5 Modes Headlight and 4 Modes Taillight-Smart Sensor,Free Mount Brackets Tool I received this as a review sample and want to disclose up front that the actual light is a small unit measuring approximately 1.5x2.25 inches. As small is it is the amount of illumination is incredible.

Since the product specs and some of the previous reviews cover this in great detail I will try to fill in the cracks and provide [hopefully] useful information that others missed.

First, the 'O' rings mentioned are not for sealing, but affixing the light to handlebars and the headband that ships with this light. The velcro strap is for the battery pack. I think the design of the 'O' rings in particular is clever, but do be aware that they are easy to lose and if you drop one on a dark surface in the rain it will be hard to find even using the strong illumination from this light. I know this because it actually happened.

The light runs a little hot, but the fins, which are heat sinks, prevent it from burning you. I recommend waiting a few minutes after turning it off before removing it from the hear band or handlebars.

I cannot validate the waterproof claim since there is no IP rating given at the time of this review. It will certainly work in the rain and other wet environments, but as for submerging the unit and the depth to which it can remain waterproof I have no idea. The battery pack connector looks waterproof and certainly worked in a heavy rain, and the light itself is thoroughly sealed.

If there is one lament it's the lack of instructions. For example, the 'O' ring and velcro strap took a few minutes to figure out. However, that is not a show stopper and this is not an overly complex piece of gear.

Bottom line: this is portable enough to fit in a shirt pocket (the light unit anyway - the battery pack will not), and throws an incredible amount if illumination. The main value is it can be used as a bike light as well as on the headband for a variety of uses.

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Breakfast and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply Everyday Meals 4 Gallon Pail & Butter Powder 2 lbs 4 oz No. 10 Can I'm buying calories. I am buying calories to tuck away for use after all other calories have been consumed. I have this and know it is available. I dont need to worry about it. It is there as part of my "calorie savings account". Not worried about taste, not worried about anything other than calories- preferably a variety of flavors with a good ratio of macros (fat, protein, carbohydrates). Emergency food is what it is, and what it will be. With increasing prices, todays caloric purchase is a savings over tomorrows.

So no, I haven't tried it. I HAVE used other Augason Farms products for daily life use and have been pleased. I regularly buy Augason Farms (best price point, best sales). I have tried those items only because the sale price was better than buying non emergency packed food items. I use a lot of tomato powder, dehydrated vegetables, protein crumbles, etc.. and once in awhile a sale will work in my favor. That is when I will buy 2 of something. One for now, one for way later. Rinse and repeat.

Certain food items have at least 25 year shelf life, some items are 10 years. No matter, I will eat it all 30 years down the line if need be. Foods dont just go "bad". The date is not a safety issue. It is a quality issue. So maybe the smell, taste, texture, or vitamin content alters a little over time, but it is still edible. Calories are still there.

If you want to be sure of a tasty meal that is within the best by date range, then simple stack your pantry with foods that you know and love. Rotate. Have a "working pantry" that you grab from on a daily basis, then have a "storage pantry" that works as your own in home "store". It also serves as your emergency preps. When you need to pull from your storage pantry, be sure to replace. Keep adding to it, one or two cans at a time. one or two bags of something at a time. Emergency food does not need to be emergency packaged food (prices are higher for the packaging, uniformity, processing etc). If "emergency" packaged food is outside your budget, then dont bother. If it is something you are keen on, then look for sales regularly (maybe daily) and buy when the good price strikes. Of course, you can look into creating your own long term storage meals too (mylar, oxy absorbers, pails, etc).

Just.. have something. Dont be someone who has bare shelves and scoffs at preparedness because emergency meals taste bad. Nah, buy what is good to you, buy what is affordable to you, buy basic stuff or buy fancy emergency stuff. But have stuff. Prices aren't coming down, prices will continue to go up, food will be harder to come by. So at the very least consider it an investment. And if there is a true need for it in terms of *vaguely gestures around* all else that is going on (weather events, political events, ww3, etc) then you wont be scrambling, begging off neighbors, stealing, etc.

So current $60 for nearly 20,000 calories of a variety of food? Not too shabby in light of everything. (same $60 can buy a lot more calories, but be sure to store well for max "freshness").
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Breakfast and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply Everyday Meals 4 Gallon Pail & Butter Powder 2 lbs 4 oz No. 10 Can

Raqpak Beach/Picnic Blanket, Lightweight and Sand Proof with 4 Stakes, 7 x 7 Feet The picnic blanket that we have used for years is a classic red and white checker pattern vinyl rectangle. It's fine for small outings and it does provide a moisture barrier but it is small and not suitable for more than just one or two people. This is a very different blanket, suitable for picnics and for the beach and much better suited for larger groups.

Unlike a terrycloth blanket or a vinyl sheet, this blanket is made of parachute nylon which has the advantages of being very lightweight and water resistant. It also is very non-bulky and folds up into a small and compact bundle in the *attached* bag, to a size that is slightly smaller than the average purse. I would not have thought it would pack this small, but it's absolutely perfect for packing for a trip.

When completely unfolded this blanket is 7'x7', more than adequate for a group of 4-6 people. Being as light as it is, without anchoring at the corners it can easily get caught in the wind and blow around. So, each corner has a small elastic loop and included with the blanket is a set of 4 small stakes so that it can be better anchored down. Additionally, there are pockets on the corners so that additional weight can be added (rocks or sand) which helps even more when the ground is not suitable for relying solely on stakes. The packing bag doubles as a stash bag for things like sunglasses or a phone or it can be used to hold trash items until it's time to pack up again.

Though this is marketed predominantly a blanket it is more useful to me and to my family as a table cloth for picnic tables. Skyline Drive in Shenandoah National Park has several picnic areas that are wonderful places to stop and spend time for lunch and this blanket covers those picnic tables nicely. The packing bag again serves double duty - it works well for holding utensils (spoons, ladles, etc.) while the blanket is spread on the table and it can again hold small amounts of trash until packing up to leave.

This blanket is a very simple but very nice product that serves multiple purposes. It's fine for use on the beach and it works just for as a picnic blanket but it's just as useful as a picnic table cover. It packs up very nicely and is extremely portable and is not unreasonably priced.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: Raqpak Beach/Picnic Blanket, Lightweight and Sand Proof with 4 Stakes, 7 x 7 Feet

Viper by GLD Products 800 Regulation Size Electronic Dartboard, Featuring 57 Game options for up to 16 players, Enhanced Scoring Experience with Ultra-Thin Spider, and Top Quality Segments to Reduce Bounce Outs, Black I was pleasantly surprised at how well this dartboard works and how many different game options it offers. I am old school and prefer to just play the basic game but, the kids all love playing all the other game options this board offers. Keeps them busy and entertained for hours.
Can either play against the computer for a lot of practice or you can play against other players.
First observation is the darts. They're nice and light so they don't do any damage to my walls if a wild dart is thrown. They're cheap and will break but you can easily replace these, if they do break. I like keeping the cheaper darts out for the kids to play with. The darts are held right onto the board so there's no searching around for them. Not saying the kids will put the darts in the right spot when done playing but, it's a nice convenience. You can also upgrade your darts to the heavier more expensive ones they sell. Warning, the heavier darts will put marks on the walls. So the better ones I keep in a case and are only used by my wife and I. The heavier ones do stick into the board a lot tighter. Best to just twist dart back and forth, like a screwdriver, and then pull it out. Haven't had any problem with my better darts breaking so far.
The game board is really well made. No problems with the darts holding in the small holes. Scoring is spot on so no issues with that at all.
I was worried about the LCD screen being hit by any darts. Especially the heavier ones I have. So, I took a thin piece of plexiglass, cut it down to the size I wanted, and attached it over the LCD display to protect it. By looking at all the small little marks on it, I'm glad I did this before we started playing with it.
Overall it's a nice dartboard game for the price. It's a great addition to our game room that doesn't take up any room at all.

text_fidelity_a:
Takeya Actives Sip Lid, Wide Mouth I am writing this review from the perspective of a Hydro Flask owner. Even though this isn't a Hydro Flask lid, it's Takeya, which is still good quality.

I hate all of the hydroflask brand lids. The twist coffee lids have tendency to failure in my opinion, the screw lids are not great if you like to take sips often, and the straw lids are actually not bad, but sometimes, you just don't want a straw. This lid is a great alternative if you want a simple one-handed open close that's still strong enough that it won't open by accident.

Pros
-easy one handed open
-if you look closely at the pictures there is a textured rubber grip that makes grabbing it from the top a more secure feeling
-the moveable handle is nice
-Many other 3rd party lids are either too tight (hard to open) or too loose (prone to accidental openings and leaks). But this one is perfectly right in the middle. It's easy to open one handed, but still fairly secure to resist accidental openings.

Cons:
Like most of these snap lids, the trade-off is slightly less insulation then the HydroFlask brand lids. When I did a side-by side test with several of my Hydro Flask lids, this Takeya melted ice faster than the hydroflask. This is still not too bad as the water was still cold, just not quite as cold as a stock hydroflask lid

Who this is for: You want a more convenient drinking experience and hate the Hydro Flask brand options. Good for one-handed open/close

Who this isn't for: If you must have long-lasting ice in your container for as much time as possible.
text_fidelity_b: Takeya Actives Sip Lid, Wide Mouth

Mountain House Chicken & Dumplings | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food |2 Servings I've had a number of these lately, testing out the different flavors to see what I would like to have in the family camping and emergency supplies stash. I have been continually surprised at how good the flavors are, and how much I enjoy eating these.

The gravy mix is at the bottom, so what you do to prepare this is you measure out your boiling water carefully and pour it in, give it a stir and close the container, wait a few minutes as specified on the package, stir and close the container again to let it finish soaking in.

In my experience, the meals rehydrate best when they are made with extremely hot boiling water, and when you make sure that you do not in any way skimp on the liquid component. I measured sloppily on one of mine, and the biscuits came out a little crunchy. I have also noticed that for my personal tastes, I prefer a longer wait time than they specify. At the beginning of my meal, the center of some of the larger chunks were not fully rehydrated, and though we were all okay with the tiny bit of crunch, the meal tasted much more like a normal meal when we were almost at the end of eating it. I was worried about letting it set too long to where it got soggy, but that didn't occur, it just got tastier with a longer soaking time.

As for the flavor of this one specifically, they really got the seasonings just right. It feels like a very comforting, homemade meal, with a nice thick chicken gravy pulling together all of the chunks.
text_fidelity_b: Mountain House Chicken & Dumplings | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food |2 Servings

I found the directions to set up this model quite easy to follow, even including the calibration for my stride length. I carry the device in either a pocket or clipped to my waist daily and have had no problems with getting a 'read' from either location. I have found that this is easy to use, and reliable. The batteries are still going strong after more than three months of daily use. The clip has kept the unit firmly attached and despite being dropped a few times, the unit keeps on working.

I would recommend this to everyone as an easy to use, inexpensive and reliable motivation to get moving.

text_fidelity_a:
Graphite Pickleball Paddles Set of 4, 2023 USAPA Approved, Carbon Fiber Surface (CHS), Polypropylene Lightweight Honeycomb Core, 3 Indoor 3 Outdoor Pickleball, 4 Replacement Soft Grip + Bag I like that this comes with its own little zippered carrying case. That's just an extra that makes it nicer than having to find a duffel-bag or some other place to carry the set.

It comes with 4 paddles that are the same except for the colors. It has 3 indoor and 3 outdoor balls which are almost identical except for the spacing of the holes. They're like Whiffle™ balls. The holes prevent them from going too far from the air resistance. The ones for indoors are the ones with the bigger holes because you can't hit them as far.

I know it says that you can play indoors and technically that's true, but it depends on where you're playing. A big game room with lots of space would work. A place where you can trip over furniture or knock over lamps isn't a good idea. It also depends on how aggressive you want to be with your swings. The indoor balls are not the problem because they couldn't easily build up enough momentum to break anything except very delicate or top-heavy things. But the paddles swinging around are more of the issue with playing indoors. A big swing or stretch if you aren't aware of the stuff around you could be where you'd break something or trip over something. But still, about the same level of caution you'd have with Ping-Pong, but without the table to keep you in place.

The paddles are pretty nice quality and lighter than they look like they should be. But they have a lot of surface area and the balls are easier to hit than with Ping-Pong paddles.

You'll have to look up the rules online because they aren't included, but really that's only if you want to play "official Pickle-ball". You can play it with Ping-pong rules, badminton rules, volleyball rules, tennis rules -- just about any of the similar kind of games that I can think of -- it's just a bit easier and has requires less skill or movement. It's really about the same level of activity that you'd have with badminton and the same sized area if you're playing outdoors.

Personally, indoors is just if we want to play "hit-the-ball-back-and-forth-down-the-hallway" because it's too hot/cold/wet outside.

This doesn't come with a net, and I thought the rubberband strips might have been to map out the court area, but it's supposed to be for the grip on the paddles. If you're going to play "official" you'll need a net which is pretty much the same as a badminton net just not as high. It's basically a mini tennis court with much the same net.

It's good exercise, and I can't imagine this being a competitive sport, but I was wrong about tag being an 'official' sport when I heard someone mention it -- but it actually is and surprisingly fun to watch -- with sponsors and everything. Pickleball might be the same because why wouldn't someone take something that's fun and add a bunch of rules so they can make some money from advertising.

It's good for staying active and just about everyone likes to play because we don't play with any real rules. Not because we have odd ideas like "there are no losers here", but because it's just that unimportant.

I can't comment on the price with the way things are these days, but it seems to be about the same price as other options, and the quality is decent. The bag is a bonus and even the dog likes to play -- but that's where it goes from being 'pickle-ball' to 'slobber-ball'.

Overall, this is a nice set, especially the paddles. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: Graphite Pickleball Paddles Set of 4, 2023 USAPA Approved, Carbon Fiber Surface (CHS), Polypropylene Lightweight Honeycomb Core, 3 Indoor 3 Outdoor Pickleball, 4 Replacement Soft Grip + Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Allen Sports Aluminum 2 Child Trailer/Single & Double Swivel Wheel Stroller This is an initial impressions commentary less than it is a review. I plan on following up once I've had at least a month's worth of activity with it. Here in Chicago, the weather has been varying at the time of this review, so we've been able to use this only about a solid week's worth.

The night I received it I assembled it immediately. I've put together a few strollers, so I didn't intend on taking longer than twenty minutes. Not with this stroller. It took me almost an hour. The instructions came in two parts: one sheet indicating that it may be difficult to unfold at first, and the main instructions. Indeed, the stroller is very difficult to unfold at first, and it is difficult to fold back.
The instructions were not very coherent; the illustrations, instead of being reference models as in most manuals, were black-and-white photographs which made it difficult to discern exactly what they were trying to portray. Half the time I was trying to figure it out, and ended up going with my gut-feeling (which, thankfully to my previous stroller assembly experiences, led me to the correct outcomes).

Unfolding it the first time proved very difficult. Again, I did this myself with the assumption that it wouldn't be very difficult, so I did have a harder than usual unfolding it into its locked position. Once everything was assembled (mind you, you will need to provide your own tools as mine came with the wrong sized hex/L wrench and was missing the other tool, whatever it was), I was ready to put it in the basement for the time being. We live in a pretty spacious apartment building with plenty of basement storage, and that's where we store all of our strollers, etc. Folding it back was pretty rough; I could not for the life of me tell where the unlocking mechanisms were due to the poorly lit photographs, so I had to figure it out. Once I got it, however, one side of the locks was very hard to unlock.

On our first walks, however, the stroll was fine. It glides pretty smoothly, but I wish the handlebar had an easier and quicker way to adjust the angle, as our previous strollers have. As I mentioned before, it's very difficult to unfold and requires two people, so when my wife tried to get the stroller out on her own she was unable to due to the force required. Who knows how this will be with time.

As I've mentioned, I will follow up with a more experienced review.
text_fidelity_b: Allen Sports Aluminum 2 Child Trailer/Single & Double Swivel Wheel Stroller
